name: Fast Bundle
summary: Shopify app that covers every bundle format from one place (fixed bundles, mix-and-match, build-your-own, BOGO, volume breaks and AI frequently-bought-together) on product pages, in the cart and in POS. Shopify pulled the app after a July 2026 security incident and relisted it on 30 July.
best_for: Shopify merchants who want every bundle and upsell format from one app (mix-and-match, build-your-own, BOGO, volume breaks, AI frequently-bought-together) priced against what those offers actually earn rather than a flat fee, and who are comfortable with an app that Shopify delisted for two weeks in July 2026 and then restored
skip_if: you need one bundle type only, where a single-purpose app costs less than the metered ladder; you sell in person, since Shopify POS support sits behind the $299 Enterprise tier; or an app in your path to checkout having been pulled and deactivated once, however well handled, is a risk you cannot carry
honest_knock:
The most important thing about this app is not on its App Store listing. On 17 July 2026 Fast Bundle detected what its own status page calls a security attack; Shopify removed the app from the App Store as a precaution and deactivated it on existing stores, so merchants found it simply gone. It was restored to limited visibility on 30 July and fully searchable again on 3 August, after Shopify reviewed an incident report and a third-party vulnerability and penetration test. The vendor states its investigation and testing found no indication that any customer, store or shopper data was accessed, exposed or leaked, and that 2,405 stores had reinstalled by early August. Shopify's own words, quoted on that page, are that the app “has been restored to limited visibility”.

Nobody outside the process can verify what was reached, and neither the vendor nor Shopify has published the technical detail. What is verifiable is the shape of the disruption: a storefront-facing app pulled without warning, deactivated on live stores, and roughly two weeks coming back. If your bundles carry your average order value, that is the risk you are underwriting, not because it is likely to recur, but because it has happened once and the app sits in the path to checkout.

The review record needs reading with that date in mind. 3,031 reviews with 3,000 at five stars against 19 at one is exceptional. But most of that history predates July 2026, and Shopify app ratings skew high because merchants are prompted for them. What an average cannot tell you is how a vendor handles an incident, and on that the status page is the better evidence: dated, specific, quoting Shopify directly, and correcting its own earlier estimates in public. That is a good sign about communication rather than about security.

One practical hazard came out of the outage and has not gone away. While the app was delisted, other apps renamed themselves to include “Fast Bundle” — the vendor names Fast Bundle Offer, BOGO, BYOB; Sparrow Fast Bundle Upsell App; and Rabbit Fast Bundle & Upsell, and Shopify subsequently delisted three of them. Searching the App Store for the name is therefore not a reliable way to find this app. Install from the listing slug, fast-bundle-product-bundles, and check that the developer reads Fast Bundle.

Finally, the listing's data grant is broad even for this category: it edits customers and customer tags, products, inventory and collections, orders including third-party fulfilment and order edits, discount codes and promotions, Shopify Functions cart transforms, the checkout page and Online Store pages. Cart transforms are how a bundle becomes a single line item, so the scope is explicable, but an app with write access to your discounts and your checkout page belongs in your processing register and in whatever review you run after an incident like July's.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Standard (1K) · per month on the App Store listing, or $180 a year, for up to $1,000 of monthly bundle-attributed sales with a 7-day free trial
pricing.notes:
(read 2026-08-24 on apps.shopify.com/fast-bundle-product-bundles, listed as “FBP | Fast Bundle & Upsell App”, and on fastbundle.co/pricing) The meter here is not your catalogue, your traffic or your seats — it is the revenue your bundles themselves generate. The listing is free to install and shows four tiers. Development stores are free to install and free to run. Standard (1K) is $19 a month or $180 a year and covers up to $1,000 of monthly bundle sales. Standard (3K) is $49 a month or $468 a year for up to $3,000. Standard (10K) is $139 a month or $1,380 a year for up to $10,000. All three paid tiers carry a 7-day free trial and the same feature list: unlimited bundles, upsells and cross-sells, mix and match, volume-discount upsell, BOGO and Buy X Get Y, unlimited AI frequently-bought-together, product add-ons, 24/7 English support and the AI bundle image generator. The App Store states all charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days.

The vendor's own pricing page adds a fifth tier the listing never shows: Enterprise at $299 a month or $2,988 a year, described as limitless monthly bundle revenue, with automatic bundle detection in the cart, Shopify POS integration, minor specialised customisations, priority onboarding with an account manager and a five-minute support target against Standard's thirty. That page also prices the annual commitments as effective monthly rates — $15, $39, $115 and $249 — under a “2-MONTHS FREE” label, and it is the only place the free plan is described in full: all six bundle types, 24/7 support, available to development stores and “eligible merchants”, and capped at $500 in bundle sales a month. Its comparison table shows what the free tier gives up: volume discounts and product add-ons on selected products only rather than collections or the whole catalogue, no AI frequently-bought-together across all products, no multilingual translation, no subscription-app integration, and a “Powered by Fast Bundle” credit left on your storefront.

Fast Bundle's own FAQ defines the metered revenue as sales through bundles, volume discounts, product add-ons, mix and match, Buy X Get Y, frequently bought together and other offers created with the app, and states that exceeding your plan's monthly bundle revenue limit means upgrading to keep campaigns running. Developer Fast Bundle, listed at 13353 Commerce Parkway, Unit 2353, Richmond, BC, Canada; the app launched on 26 November 2020, the vendor's site claims 22,400 merchants, and the listing carried 3,031 reviews at a 5.0 average at the time of writing. Re-read 10 October 2026 on the listing: the three Standard prices and annual rates are unchanged, the listing now offers an optional Auto Bundle Detection add-on at +$49 a month on each Standard tier, and it carried 3,535 reviews at a 5.0 average. Re-read 20 November 2026 on the listing and on fastbundle.co/pricing: Standard (1K) $19 a month or $180 a year, Standard (3K) $49 or $468, Standard (10K) $139 or $1,380, the optional Auto Bundle Detection add-on at +$49 a month, Enterprise at $299 a month or $2,988 a year and the free plan's $500 monthly bundle-sales cap are all unchanged; the listing carried 3,688 reviews at a 5.0 average.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 16 November 2026 the session tested Fast Bundle on the Free plan of a Shopify development store: a fixed bundle of two snowboards at 10 percent off, the extra step of switching on the app embed, the plan screens up to the Shopify approval screen and the uninstall dialog. Nothing was paid, approved or uninstalled. Select bundle type lists Fixed bundle (marked Best match), Volume discounts, Buy X Get Y | Free gift, Mix and match, Bundle builder, Product add-ons, Cross-sell (Beta) and Frequently bought together, all in the same app. In Create Fixed bundle the default discount is Percentage 10 and the status Active. We chose The Collection Snowboard: Liquid ($749.95) and The Compare at Price Snowboard ($785.95), quantity 1 each, and left the name; the app named it Bundle #1. The app preview showed $1,535.90 struck through and $1,382.31 for 10% off; the default presentation is separate line items. After Save the app said the bundle was created and showed a yellow message: the bundle is saved but only appears in the store once the app embed is switched on. That is a required extra step: the button opened the theme editor, where the Fast Bundle switch was already on, and after Save it said Fast Bundle activated and Changes saved. Shopify now holds a product Bundle Product #1, status Active, vendor Fast Bundle, type snowboard. The store is password protected and the password was not entered, so the bundle was only seen in the theme editor preview of /products/bundle-product-1: the title, Fast Bundle, $1,535.90 struck through, $1,382.31, the label Sale, the two snowboards with their prices and Add to cart. No order or checkout was made. The app home afterwards showed App embed status Active, App block status 0 active blocks, Bundle views 3, Bundle clicks 0 and Total sales value $0.00. Timing, approximate tester observations: install click at 13:57, app open at 13:57:45, bundle saved at 13:58:45 and visible in the preview at 14:00:07; about 2 minutes 20 seconds from the app opening to the preview, the bundle itself saved after about 1 minute, and about 10 clicks (Install, Create bundle, Select Fixed bundle, Select products, 2 ticks, Add, Save, switch on the app embed, Save in the theme editor). Buy X Get Y and volume discount exist as bundle types and in the plan table (Buy X Get Y is ticked on all plans; volume discount on specific products is ticked on Free, volume discount on all products and collections is not on Free but on Standard and Enterprise); they were not built. Uninstall: the More actions menu with Uninstall app opened a dialog with a reason list and a feedback box that was cancelled; what remains after removal, such as the bundle product and the embed, was not seen. The Plans page ends with a box Subscription cancellation, if you want to cancel your subscription just click here; it was not clicked because there was no subscription. Not tested: building a Buy X Get Y or volume discount bundle, a bundle on a public store page or in the cart and checkout, an approved subscription or trial, the yearly prices in the app, support and chat. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: A saved bundle does not show in the store until the app embed is switched on, which is a second step in the theme editor, and the store password kept the bundle out of a public view.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 16 November 2026 the session tested Fast Bundle on the Free plan of a Shopify development store: a fixed bundle of two snowboards at 10 percent off, the extra step of switching on the app embed, the plan screens up to the Shopify approval screen and the uninstall dialog. Nothing was paid, approved or uninstalled. Select bundle type lists Fixed bundle (marked Best match), Volume discounts, Buy X Get Y | Free gift, Mix and match, Bundle builder, Product add-ons, Cross-sell (Beta) and Frequently bought together, all in the same app. In Create Fixed bundle the default discount is Percentage 10 and the status Active. We chose The Collection Snowboard: Liquid ($749.95) and The Compare at Price Snowboard ($785.95), quantity 1 each, and left the name; the app named it Bundle #1. The app preview showed $1,535.90 struck through and $1,382.31 for 10% off; the default presentation is separate line items. After Save the app said the bundle was created and showed a yellow message: the bundle is saved but only appears in the store once the app embed is switched on. That is a required extra step: the button opened the theme editor, where the Fast Bundle switch was already on, and after Save it said Fast Bundle activated and Changes saved. Shopify now holds a product Bundle Product #1, status Active, vendor Fast Bundle, type snowboard. The store is password protected and the password was not entered, so the bundle was only seen in the theme editor preview of /products/bundle-product-1: the title, Fast Bundle, $1,535.90 struck through, $1,382.31, the label Sale, the two snowboards with their prices and Add to cart. No order or checkout was made. The app home afterwards showed App embed status Active, App block status 0 active blocks, Bundle views 3, Bundle clicks 0 and Total sales value $0.00. Timing, approximate tester observations: install click at 13:57, app open at 13:57:45, bundle saved at 13:58:45 and visible in the preview at 14:00:07; about 2 minutes 20 seconds from the app opening to the preview, the bundle itself saved after about 1 minute, and about 10 clicks (Install, Create bundle, Select Fixed bundle, Select products, 2 ticks, Add, Save, switch on the app embed, Save in the theme editor). Buy X Get Y and volume discount exist as bundle types and in the plan table (Buy X Get Y is ticked on all plans; volume discount on specific products is ticked on Free, volume discount on all products and collections is not on Free but on Standard and Enterprise); they were not built. Uninstall: the More actions menu with Uninstall app opened a dialog with a reason list and a feedback box that was cancelled; what remains after removal, such as the bundle product and the embed, was not seen. The Plans page ends with a box Subscription cancellation, if you want to cancel your subscription just click here; it was not clicked because there was no subscription. Not tested: building a Buy X Get Y or volume discount bundle, a bundle on a public store page or in the cart and checkout, an approved subscription or trial, the yearly prices in the app, support and chat. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: A saved bundle does not show in the store until the app embed is switched on, which is a second step in the theme editor, and the store password kept the bundle out of a public view.
